title: The Campaign to Bring Jensen Back
summary: Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, and its chips power much of the artificial intelligence boom. So when its co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down last week, it made waves across Silicon Valley. Now a campaign wants him back. More than 175,000 people have signed an open letter asking Nvidia's board to give Huang his job back. The campaign, called Bring Jensen Back, says it was launched by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters. They say Huang was removed without meaningful due process. The campaign has some very famous backers. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he would certainly not mind seeing Huang reinstated. Elon Musk, the head of SpaceX, and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. But Nvidia itself is not budging. The company has dismissed the campaign, and the Financial Times reported that Huang has been discussing a possible return with confidants, though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him. A representative for Huang declined to comment. The story has also stirred debate in Washington. The White House said on Monday that it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. For now, the boardroom battle continues, with a petition, a president and some of tech's biggest names all pulling in different directions.
why_it_matters: Nvidia's chips power the artificial intelligence in phones, games and computers, so who runs the company can shape the technology children use every day.
